latest_release.name: v0.25.1
latest_release.body:
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/compare/v0.25.0...v0.25.1

This release stops credentials and cookies from following redirects to another site. Upgrading is recommended.

## Security

### Credentials no longer follow redirects to another origin

An `Authorization` header, `basic_auth` and `digest_auth` are now only sent to the same scheme, host and port they were given for, as in curl, Python requests and browsers. An http → https upgrade on the default ports keeps them. (#819, #915, thanks @davefej)

Before, credentials could reach another server in these cases:

| Redirect | `Authorization` in `headers:` | `basic_auth` |
|---|---|---|
| To a different host | sent | dropped |
| Scheme-relative (`//other.example.com/x`) | sent | sent |
| `https://` → `http://` on the same host | sent unencrypted | sent unencrypted |
| Same host, different port | sent | sent |

`digest_auth` also answered a 401 challenge from the host it was redirected to. All of these now drop the credentials. A redirect on the same host, or an http → https upgrade, still sends them.

### Cookies no longer follow redirects to another origin

Cookies from `headers:`, the `cookies:` option, class-level `cookies` and the previous host's `Set-Cookie` were sent to any host a redirect pointed at. HTTParty doesn't track the cookie `Domain` attribute, so on a redirect to a different scheme, host or port it now sends none of them. Cookies the new host sets are kept for its own later redirects. (#916)

If a single request relies on a `Domain=.example.com` cookie reaching a sibling subdomain through a redirect (say `login.example.com` → `app.example.com`), that cookie is no longer sent.

### Log lines can't be forged through the request path

`ApacheFormatter` escapes control characters, `"` and `\` in the request path as Apache's own access log does (`\x0d\x0a`), so a crafted path can't split or forge a log line. This only applies with a permissive URI adapter such as Addressable; the default adapter already rejects these characters. (#892, #914, thanks @fuzzyrichie)

## Bug Fixes

- Cookies set by a same-origin redirect are sent along with your class and request cookies. Before, they replaced them, which could drop a session cookie on an ordinary redirect. (#916)
- When a redirect turns a request into a GET, HTTParty no longer sends the headers that described the dropped body (`Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding`, `Content-Language`, `Content-Location`). (#696, #867, thanks @wleeaf)
- A `body_stream` is dropped along with the body when a redirect turns the request into a GET. Before, the GET resent the already-read stream, which raised `ArgumentError` or went out chunked. (#917)
- The curl log format no longer raises on UTF-16 or UTF-7 bodies, or on a non-ASCII header or query key with a binary value. (#848, #850, thanks @ethanstoner)
- Responses declaring a Ruby "dummy" charset (UTF-7, UTF-32, ISO-2022-JP, IBM037) parse instead of raising `Encoding::CompatibilityError`. (#912)

## Other

- Gems built on Linux no longer include the spec and feature files. (#911)
- Fixed four documentation examples that raised when run. (#913)
- Added a cucumber scenario for relative redirects. (#918)

detail.readme:
# httparty

[![CI](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Makes http fun again! Ain't no party like a httparty, because a httparty don't stop.

## Install

```
gem install httparty
```

## Requirements

- Ruby 2.7.0 or higher
- You like to party!

## Examples

```ruby
# Use the class methods to get down to business quickly
response = HTTParty.get('https://api.stackexchange.com/2.2/questions?site=stackoverflow')

puts response.body, response.code, response.message, response.headers.inspect

# Or wrap things up in your own class
class StackExchange
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'api.stackexchange.com'

  def initialize(service, page)
    @options = { query: { site: service, page: page } }
  end

  def questions
    self.class.get("/2.2/questions", @options)
  end

  def users
    self.class.get("/2.2/users", @options)
  end
end

stack_exchange = StackExchange.new("stackoverflow", 1)
puts stack_exchange.questions
puts stack_exchange.users
```

See the [examples directory](http://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/tree/main/examples) for even more goodies.

## Command Line Interface

httparty also includes the executable `httparty` which can be
used to query web services and examine the resulting output. By default
it will output the response as a pretty-printed Ruby object (useful for
grokking the structure of output). This can also be overridden to output
formatted XML or JSON. Execute `httparty --help` for all the
options. Below is an example of how easy it is.

```
httparty "https://api.stackexchange.com/2.2/questions?site=stackoverflow"
```

## Help and Docs

- [Docs](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/tree/main/docs)
- https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/discussions
- https://www.rubydoc.info/github/jnunemaker/httparty

## Contributing

- Fork the project.
- Run `bundle`
- Run `bundle exec rake`
- Make your feature addition or bug fix.
- Add tests for it. This is important so I don't break it in a future version unintentionally.
- Run `bundle exec rake` (No, REALLY :))
- Commit, do not mess with rakefile, version, or history. (if you want to have your own version, that is fine but bump version in a commit by itself in another branch so I can ignore when I pull)
- Send me a pull request. Bonus points for topic branches.
